newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CONTINUES FALLING ON UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CONTINUES FALLING ON UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted weaker on hard units in early Friday trade, with foreign exchange dealers predicting it would depreciate further during the day.
"The main concern in the market is the rate of depreciation. Everyday we're losing one to two cents (on the key U.S. dollar) and it doesn't augur well for our market," one dealer said.

"We've seen the Reserve Bank coming in but in very thin volumes and it didn't do much for the dollar. Indications are that the market is still short, even though there are no very big payments," he added.
"The only way to stop the depreciation is for the central bank to come in in a big way......and stabilise the market," the
At around 0800 GMT the Zimbabwe dollar was trading at 11.1125/1225 against the U.S. unit after closing on Thursday at 11.1025/1125 and fell to 17.8975/9255 from 17.8775/9055 against sterling.
It was also quoted easier on the mark at 6.6100/6200 compared to 6.5955/6050 and at 2.4850/4900 from 2.4770/4810 versus the rand.
